headline: Held public hearing on 2025 CAPER report and continued work on syringe litter recommendations, with another meeting set for October 6th
summary: The committee held a public hearing on the City's 2025 Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER), which covers HUD CDBG and HOME funding from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Members also discussed recommendations from the syringe litter report, including harm reduction definitions, SeeClickFix reporting changes, and support for needle stick victims. The committee agreed to hold an additional meeting on October 6th and continue the discussion at its regular meeting on October 21st.
decisions: Continued work on the syringe litter report recommendations to an additional meeting on October 6th and the regular meeting on October 21st.

decision_evidence.quote: The committee agreed to schedule an additional meeting on October 6th at 6:00 PM and their regular meeting on October 21st to continue working on the recommendations.

CDNR Committee Meeting 
Wednesday, September 16, 2026 
6:00 – 8:00 PM 
Sharon Bushor Conference Room, 1st Floor – City Hall 
 
Committee members: Evan Litwin (EL), Allie Schachter (AS), Laura Sanchez-Parkinson (LSP), 
Carter Neubieser (CN) 
City Staff: Christine Curtis, CEDO 
Other Attendees:  Maggie Callaghan, Alex Fox, CEDO 
 
Draft Minutes 
 
Meeting Started at 6:00 PM 
 
1. Approve agenda   
MOTION by Councilor Schachter, SECOND by Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson, 
to approve the agenda 
VOTING: unanimous; motion carries. 
 
2. Adopt Minutes   
MOTION by Councilor Schachter, SECOND by Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson, 
to approve the 9/3/26 minutes 
VOTING: unanimous; motion carries. 
 
 
 
CITY OF BURLINGTON, VERMONT 
CITY COUNCIL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & 
NEIGHBORHOOD REVITALIZATION COMMITTEE 
c/o Community & Economic Development Office 
City Hall, Room 32 • 149 Church Street • Burlington, VT 05401 
802-865-7144 VOX • 802-865-7024 FAX • www.burlingtonvt.gov/cedo
3. Public Forum  
• Bella Fearn, Ed Baker, Chris McGrath, Andre Clark spoke during public 
forum 
• Public comment was received on harm reduction and syringe litter, 
with support for an Overdose Prevention Center and community 
cleanup efforts 
 
4. Public Hearing: 2025 Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation 
Report (CAPER) – CEDO 
• The meeting focused on presenting the City of Burlington's 2025 
Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER), 
which evaluates funding from HUD, including Community 
Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Home Investment Partnership 
Program (HOME) funds. Maggie Callahan and Alex Fox from the 
Community Economic Development Office explained that the report 
covers activities from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2026, and discussed 
the new NRSA (Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area) targeting 
the Old North End, with approximately 34% of CDBG funds allocated 
to this area. The team noted they are currently in a public comment 
period that ends September 25th, after which the final report will be 
submitted to HUD on September 28th. 
• Christine explained that while there is no fixed target percentage for 
serving NRSA-eligible individuals, the program aims to align with 
annual action plan projections, which have shown a slight increase to 
approximately 34% this year. The CDBG Advisory Board, which 
includes ward representatives, is intended to report back to their 
NPA communities about awarded projects and CAPER information, 
though this practice is not consistently followed. The HOME program 
operates on a rolling basis with applications accepted year-round 
through a common application system, while CDBG follows a 
structured process with NOFA releases in December and applications 
due by January. 
• AS discussed outreach efforts for community engagement, with AS 
planning to leverage advisory committees and Trusted Community 
Voices to spread awareness about grant opportunities. Christine 
noted that while fewer CDBG applications were received this year 
due to federal funding constraints, some new applicants were 
successfully funded for the first time in several years. The meeting
included a public hearing on the CAPER report where a question was 
asked about micro-enterprise definitions, which were clarified as 
businesses with 5 or fewer employees where the owner or 51% of 
employees must be low-to-moderate income.  
 
5. Continued Discussion on Syringe Litter Report 
• The committee discussed the report on syringe litter, with CN 
expressing concerns about the completeness of recommendations 
and suggesting the need for dedicated city staff to address the issue. 
EL and AS clarified that the Board of Health report had already been 
thoroughly reviewed by the committee last summer, and while it 
included recommendations for expanding syringe cleanup boxes and 
partnering with community organizations, it did not specifically call 
for dedicated city staff. The committee then moved to discuss 
actionable recommendations, starting with adopting a citywide 
definition of harm reduction principles that would incorporate 
diverse stakeholder needs. 
• The committee discussed recommendations regarding syringe 
disposal and harm reduction. They agreed that CDNR should convene 
a group of stakeholders to develop a definition of harm reduction 
and recovery as a holistic approach. For the second recommendation 
about syringe disposal notices, the committee preferred re-wording 
it to focus on education and suggested working with existing 
organizations like AHS and Vermont Cares that already have best 
practices in place. The discussion highlighted the need to consolidate 
some of the 18 recommendations in the report to make them more 
achievable. 
• The meeting focused on discussing SeeClickFix reporting 
improvements for syringe litter, with AS supporting two key 
recommendations: adding a quantitative box to report the number of 
needles and encouraging public submissions for better tracking. Bella 
raised concerns about needing more support for responding to 
SeeClickFix reports, noting that many reports are already resolved 
before city staff can address them. The group discussed potentially 
transferring responsibility to the Board of Health and providing 
formal operational support to volunteer groups, though CN 
expressed caution about being too prescriptive in supporting 
community efforts.
• The committee discussed recommendations regarding syringe 
disposal and safety, with EL sharing his experience distributing 
grabber tools to help collect needles. LSP expressed concerns about 
data requests to the Department of Health, suggesting they focus on 
preventative and educational measures instead. The group agreed to 
remove specific recommendations for Department of Health audits 
and needle stick reporting systems, while maintaining support for 
acknowledging the real health impacts of syringe litter incidents. EL 
proposed adding a recommendation for the Department of Health to 
explore providing resources and support for accidental syringe stick 
victims, particularly noting a case where a worker contracted 
hepatitis after being stuck by a needle while working. 
• The committee agreed to schedule an additional meeting on October 
6th at 6:00 PM and their regular meeting on October 21st to 
continue working on the recommendations. They decided to reach 
out to Director Bill Ward for input on SeeClickFix, with LSP and AS 
offering to connect with him if he cannot attend the October 6th 
meeting. 
 
6. Adjournment   
• ADJOURN at 8:17 p.m. by Councilor Litwin with no objection
